A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDGE study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original exhaustive class-order evaluations, RS-versus-EDGE experiments on CIL benchmarks, and encoder-configuration analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original model-ranking, alternative-sampler, sampling-budget, and medical-image similarity results.

M1.justification: Section D.3.2 introduces a tested input-processing adaptation: GPT-5 expands medical class names into visual captions before CLIP encoding. The core EDGE sequence-generation algorithms and easy/random/hard evaluation procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section D.3.2 adds EyePACS retinal images and HAM10000 skin-lesion images, substantially extending domain coverage beyond the retained natural-image benchmarks. These datasets support text-image similarity analyses, not end-to-end medical CIL evaluations. ImageNet-A is mentioned only as supported software coverage.

E2.justification: v1 compares EDGE against RS. New Table A10 additionally evaluates Adversarial Sampling, Max-cover Sampling, single-round LLM generation, and five-round LLM refinement across six CIL learners, substantially broadening the sequence-generation comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include ranking evaluations using a randomly selected six-class subset, text-image alignment metrics, sampling-budget sweeps from 3 to 40 sequences, and extensive CUB random-order evaluations. These extend the evaluation design; the previously documented training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds class-subset robustness checks for model rankings, text-versus-image similarity analyses, a medical-label caption ablation, and sampling-budget and tail-coverage studies in Sections D.1.3 and D.3–D.5. These investigate limitations and robustness questions beyond v1's encoder-configuration analysis.

E5.justification: v2 adds Spearman correlation p-values for the medical analyses and specifies seed 42 for the class-subset replication. Figure A7 reports 600 L2P and 400 EASE random-order evaluations. These concern new studies; the existing normality tests and original three order seeds are retained.

E6.justification: Tables A5–A10 and Figures A6–A7 add rankings, benchmark statistics, alignment results, sampler comparisons, and sampling-budget findings. For example, Table A10 reports L2P hard/easy accuracies of 58.35/72.13 for EDGE versus 62.58/66.21 for RS. Figure 2a–b also changes plotted accuracies, while Tables 1–2 and A3–A4 retain their values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemmas 1–2, Theorems 1–4, and their proofs are retained across the main text and Appendices B–C. Reformatting and relocation do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims about RS limitations, similarity-guided extreme sequences, and improved distributional evaluation. The expanded conclusion restates these claims rather than changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: New discussion explains why technical medical labels can fail as visual-similarity proxies and how captions mitigate this limitation. Sections D.2–D.5 also develop deployment-dependent model-selection tradeoffs, alternative samplers' cost and transferability limitations, and circumstances in which larger RS budgets narrow EDGE's advantage.

D1.justification: New Appendix E documents PILOT/PyCIL integration, dependencies, execution commands, configuration controls, and registration of additional datasets. Section D.3.2 supplies the caption-generation model and prompt. These substantially extend v1's code link and general hyperparameter disclosure, although D.5 references an absent Appendix E.5.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2025), Exploring Open-world Continual Learning with Knowns-Unknowns Knowledge Transfer, to the introduction and references. The related-work taxonomy and central research positioning remain substantially unchanged; citation-style conversion is presentational.

P1.justification: Most retained exposition remains substantially verbatim. v2 expands the conclusion, adds acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements, introduces an appendix roadmap, and organizes the new appendix material into dedicated subsections. This is a limited revision of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables A5–A10 and Figures A4–A7, including fitted-distribution overlays, sampling-budget curves, and histograms. Figure 2 changes axis limits and legend placement, while the conference template reformats tables and page layout. Some new plots redisplay existing distributions with additional estimates.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps in v1's comparison against three random orders by testing alternative samplers, larger sampling budgets, and the CLIP similarity assumption. The medical-domain qualifications and practical reproduction guide substantially improve applicability assessment and usability. Some new experimental details remain incomplete, including the reference to nonexistent Appendix E.5, but the added scrutiny of central assumptions provides a clear net quality gain.
